content:
Last month, I completed my internship with the Law Division at NITI Aayog (15th July – 15th August 2026), and I can say with certainty that it was one of the most eye-opening phases of my law school journey so far.

Being at India's premier policy think tank gave me a front-row seat to how law actually shapes policy, and not just the other way around. A good part of my time went into researching and writing a report on how e-filing is transforming access to justice in India, exploring it not just as a technical shift but as something that genuinely changes how ordinary people experience the justice system. Alongside that, I got to work on some fairly substantial areas of law, from insolvency and cross-border proceedings under the IBC, to the recent amendments to the Code, to questions around competition law, society registrations, and even patent reform. It was a lot to take in, but every bit of it shaped how I think about law today.

None of this would have been half as meaningful without the people who guided me through it. I'm deeply grateful to Dr. Banusri Velpandian ma'am, Senior Specialist (Legal) at NITI Aayog, for her patience, constant guidance, and for pushing me to think more critically about the work I was doing. A big thank you as well to Shivani Srivastava ma'am and ADV. Abhishek Vaidya sir, for always being around to help, explain, and point me in the right direction whenever I got stuck.

More than anything, this internship showed me how much thought, effort, and people go into policy making, and that's a perspective I'll carry with me.
